item.title: Counterexamples to the Monotone Completeness Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.27184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combining a modification of the recent counterexample to the quasitrace conjecture with model-theoretic reductions due to the first author, we exhibit a counterexample to the monotone completeness conjecture. We fully reproduce the disproof of the quasitrace conjecture by a modified construction and arguments.
item.dc:creator: Jananan Arulseelan, James E. Hanson

item.title: On counterexamples to the unification of free entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.27243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been a long-standing open problem to determine when two versions of Voiculescu's free entropy, $\chi$ and $\chi^*$, agree. OpenAI recently generated the first example with $-\infty < \chi < \chi^*$. We give a detailed presentation of a similar example, and explicitly show the separation between free Fisher information and the large-$n$ limit of classical Fisher information through the relationship with Wasserstein distance. We thus situate the example in the context of probability theory and information geometry.
item.dc:creator: David Jekel

item.title: A boundary approach to rigidity of $q$-Araki--Woods factors
item.description: arXiv:2610.27520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study structural and rigidity properties of $q$-Araki--Woods factors arising from strongly continuous orthogonal representations of $\R$. We first introduce an AO-type boundary property that is formulated in terms of length projections on the $q$-Fock spaces, and prove that all $q$-Araki--Woods factors satisfy this condition. We next characterize uniform convergence of the associated malleable deformations. We then use these two ingredients as a substitute for weak containment in the coarse bimodule and deduce several rigidity theorems in the framework of Popa's deformation/rigidity theory. As a main consequence, we prove that every $q$-Araki--Woods factor is stably strongly solid. We also prove a normalizer rigidity theorem for inclusions arising from direct sum representations. Finally, we compute Connes' $\tau$-invariant, and construct a continuum of pairwise non-isomorphic type $\mathrm{III}_1$ $q$-Araki--Woods factors with the same $\tau$-invariant.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Isono

item.title: Random $C^*$-subalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.28295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a discrete countable group $\Gamma$, we introduce the concept of random subalgebras of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(\Gamma)$. This extends the existing theory of invariant random subgroups and the one of invariant random subalgebras of the group von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}(\Gamma)$. As applications, we provide a characterisation of $C^*$-simplicity, a condition for amenability of the group and show the existence and uniqueness of a maximal nuclear $\Gamma$-invariant unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$. Moreover, we give a topological characterisation of exactness of any separable unital $C^*$-algebra. Finally, we study exotic random subalgebras of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$ and super-exotic random subalgebras of ${\rm L}(\Gamma)$, that is, random subalgebras which do not arise purely from random subgroups of $\Gamma$ and not from random subalgebras of $C^*_r(\Gamma)$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Fima, Hanna Oppelmayer, Leyan Tao

item.title: C*-selflessness and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for Thompson's group $F$
item.description: arXiv:2610.28473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the reduced C*-algebra of Thompson's group $F$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bruce, Shirly Geffen

item.title: A single generation theorem for simple unital $C^*$-algebras with CPoU and comparison
item.description: arXiv:2610.28478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, assuming the finite factor generation theorem obtained by OpenAI, we demonstrate that if a separable simple unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ with nonempty trace space, has the strict comparison for positive elements, and its uniform tracial completion has complemented partitions of unity (CPoU), then $A$ is singly generated.
item.dc:creator: Xin Ma

item.title: Single commutators in Schatten ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.27024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove that every operator in the Schatten $p$-class ($p>2$) can be realized as a single commutator of operators in the Schatten $2p$-class. This settles the Pearcy-Topping question for Schatten ideals. We also obtain simultaneous operator and Schatten norm bounds for the factors.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Liu, Shanshan Yang

item.title: Triviality of $K$-homology classes of Euler characteristic operators of stratified pseudomanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.27476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the $K$-homology classes of the Euler characteristic operators associated with the minimal and maximal ideal boundary conditions of the de Rham differential on the regular part of a connected compact Thom-Mather stratified pseudomanifold, equipped with an adapted metric, are trivial beyond their indices. These indices are the Euler characteristics of the corresponding $L^2$-cohomologies. This generalizes a result of J. Rosenberg for manifolds. The proof uses Witten deformation of the de Rham operator associated with a stratified Morse function, following the work of \'Alvarez L\'opez and Calaza.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadali Aligholi

item.title: Thompson's group $F$ is not weakly amenable
item.description: arXiv:2610.27932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F$ be Thompson's group, and let $D$ be the set of dyadic rationals in $[0,1]$. We give an embedding of $\mathbb Z^{(D)}\rtimes F$ into $F$, where the semidirect product is defined by the natural action of $F$ on $D$. Using this embedding, we deduce from the nonamenability of $F$ that $F$ is not weakly amenable.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara

item.title: Isometries between C$^*$-algebras with finite corank
item.description: arXiv:2607.13367v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a characterization of linear isometries with finite corank between two arbitrary unital C$^*$-algebras in terms of Jordan $^*$-homomorphisms and ``finite-dimensional remainders''. Also, the corresponding results are given for linear isometries and linear order embeddings between self-adjoint parts of C$^*$-algebras. In the finite-dimensional case, we give new examples of linear isometries between matrix algebras.
item.dc:creator: Michiya Mori

item.title: Coarse rigidity in von Neumann algebras via derivations
item.description: arXiv:2609.26496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the interaction between amenability and first cohomology into tempered representations of groups, we propose a notion of relative coarse rigidity for $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras through modular derivations and their associated GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups. This extends Peterson's framework of $L^2$-rigidity to the nontracial setting. Our main result shows that the absence of relatively amenable summands forces the associated deformations to converge on relative commutants in ultrapowers. For diffuse von Neumann algebras with separable predual, this yields a dichotomy between the presence of an amenable summand and rigidity in terms of central sequences. Combining this principle with mixing and compactness, we provide a novel unified approach for proving indecomposability properties such as fullness, primeness and stable solidity. Applications yield new examples of relatively $\omega$-solid and relatively stably solid type III von Neumann algebras arising from amalgamated free products, operator-valued free Araki-Woods constructions, cocycle crossed products, and twisted nonsingular discrete measured groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Manish Kumar, Melchior Wirth

item.title: Kubo-Ando Means of Finite Order over Real Division Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2605.27707v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study Kubo-Ando means of finite order over the real division algebras $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{H}$. We establish an explicit bijection between Kubo-Ando means of order $n$ and normalized positive functions $f$ such that both $f$ and its transpose $f^{\top}(t)=tf(t^{-1})$ are matrix monotone of order $n$. We also prove that matrix monotonicity of a fixed order is independent of the underlying division algebra. We then investigate finite-order Kubo-Ando means under the canonical embeddings relating quaternionic, complex, and real positive definite matrices. These embeddings preserve functional calculus and the Loewner order, inducing natural correspondences between means on the original and embedded cones. We characterize their extensions to the ambient cones and study the geometry of the embeddings with respect to the Log-Euclidean metric. As an application, we obtain explicit affine formulas for Kubo-Ando means of order $2$ on $\mathscr{P}_{2}(\mathbb{D})$ and transfer them to the associated embedded cones of $4\times4$ positive definite matrices. In particular, we derive trace-determinant formulas for the geometric mean and show that they do not, in general, extend to the full ambient cones.
item.dc:creator: Jose Franco, Allan Merino

item.title: Finite-Dimensional Type I von Neumann Algebras in PyTorch: A GPU-Accelerated Framework for Random Block-Diagonal Operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.15882v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: torch_vn_algebra is a PyTorch library for numerical work with finite-dimensional von Neumann algebras, i.e. direct sums of matrix algebras. These algebras are central to operator algebra theory and, via commutants of symmetries, describe quantum systems with conserved charges or superselection rules. To our knowledge, no numerical software treats them as a data type with their centre, family of traces, conditional expectations, inclusions and functional calculus. The library fills the gap between computer algebra (exact but small-scale) and quantum simulators (large-scale but limited to Hilbert-space matrices): it handles batches of operators on CPUs and GPUs with automatic differentiation, and converts operators, states and channels. Key features: Compact tensor representation: 4D tensor (B, C, kmax, kmax), where B is batch size (e.g. Monte Carlo samples), C is the number of summands, and kmax is the max block size, enabling batched GPU processing. Lazy evaluation: matrix data materialized only on access, avoiding memory waste. Random operator generation: custom eigenvalue distributions; Haar, SU(n), COE, CSE unitary ensembles. Functional calculus and spectral methods: matrix absolute value, square root, inverse, entropy via SVD; automatic switch between exact diagonalization (block size up to 256) and power iteration for extreme eigenvalues. Three trace functionals: Tr_blunt (sum of block traces), Tr_norm (dimension-normalized), tau_vN (faithful normal tracial state). Performance: on a Tesla P100 GPU, processing 20,000 samples of 100x100 operators yields up to 30x speedup over traditional CPU workflows. Availability: open-source at https://gitlab.com/a.hobukob/von_neumann_type_i/
item.dc:creator: Irina Nikolaeva, Andrej Novikov
